title.value: Only tails matter: Average-Case Universality and Robustness in the Convex Regime
title.justification: The title of the paper indicates a focus on average-case analysis and robustness in optimization methods, specifically within the convex regime, as suggested by the phrase 'Only tails matter.'
title.quote: Only tails matter: Average-Case Universality and Robustness in the Convex Regime

extractions.description: The paper explores the average-case complexity and convergence properties of first-order optimization methods on distributions of quadratic problems. It introduces the Generalized Chebyshev method, which is optimal under certain assumptions about eigenvalue concentration. The study compares its performance to other optimization algorithms and finds that Nesterov's method is nearly optimal in the average-case. Additionally, the paper provides a theoretical framework that links the average-case performance to the Expected Spectral Distribution (e.s.d.), emphasizing the significance of eigenvalue concentration on the edges of e.s.d.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the theoretical aspects of optimization algorithms' average-case complexity and does not explicitly relate to climate change or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Recent works have studied the average convergence properties of first-order optimization methods on distributions of quadratic problems.

primary_category.quote: We argue that having a priori information on this concentration is a more grounded assumption than complete knowledge of the e.s.d. basing our analysis on the approximate concentration is effectively a middle ground between the coarseness of the worst-case scenario convergence and the restrictive previous average-case analysis.
